learningObjectives: Use the Home Menu's Save, Open, and Close commands to manage an API Scan project.
Distinguish the project-level Save/Open from the Payload's own Save/Load buttons.
Duplicate, delete, and rename folders, operations, and messages using the ribbon or context menu.
Apply the numerical-prefix naming convention so elements sort in TestCase execution order.

elements.description: Save, Open, and Close (left-hand side) manipulate the API Scan project as a whole. Duplicate, Delete, and Rename (right-hand side) manipulate individual elements of the project, such as messages or operations.

elements.title: What Save/Open/Close actually do
items: Close project — starts a new, empty API Scan project. You'll be prompted to save the current project first.
Save — saves the API project onto the hard drive as a file, regardless of whether Tosca Commander is installed. This makes it usable as a Tosca Subset file later.
Save as workspace template — also saves elements/messages as Modules in Tosca, so each message doesn't need to be added separately when imported.
Open project — reloads a previously saved project with all its values intact.
Closing the whole API Scan window (top-right X) while a scan is open also saves it, so the next time it opens it reloads automatically.

elements.text: When working in an environment where Tosca Commander is not installed (the standalone API Scan only), you cannot export the API project directly into Tosca — but you can still Save it to disk, and use that file later as a Tosca Subset.

bulletPoints: Best practice: save the API project file in the same folder as the Tosca project you're working in.
The Payload's own Save/Load buttons (bottom-right of the Payload) only save/load the CURRENT message — not the whole project.

elements.description: Highlight a folder or message and click Duplicate to create a copy in the same root folder. The copy keeps the old name with a number appended (e.g. duplicating "Ex 2" creates "Ex 3").
Highlight an element and click Delete (or press the Delete key) to remove it from the project file.

elements.text: There is no Undo in the API Scan. An accidentally deleted element cannot be recovered without re-loading the file or re-scanning the URI. Save your project regularly, or duplicate the main folder elsewhere first, as a safety net.

elements.description: Either highlight an element and click Rename in the Home Menu, or click the element and press F2. All three actions — duplicate, delete, rename — are also available from the right-click context menu on any element.

The API Scan sorts folders, payloads, messages, and components alphabetically. Because of this, best practice is to rename elements with a numerical prefix matching the order they'll be used in the TestCase — e.g. "01 Get Address", "02 Add to Cart".

bulletPoints: No Undo exists in the API Scan — save often, or duplicate before risky changes.
Numbering elements (01, 02, 03...) keeps the alphabetically-sorted list in logical TestCase order.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing project Save/Open with Payload Save/Load
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think the Save/Load buttons in the bottom-right of the Payload save the whole API Scan project.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Home Menu Save/Open manage the ENTIRE project. The Payload's own Save/Load buttons only save or load the CURRENT message being viewed (request or response).

examPitfalls.title: Expecting an Undo function
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates delete an element in the API Scan and try Ctrl+Z to bring it back.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: There is no Undo in the API Scan. A deleted element can only be recovered by reloading the saved file or re-scanning the URI — save regularly to protect against mistakes.

examPitfalls.title: Leaving elements unnumbered
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates leave Operations/Messages with their original scanned names, resulting in an alphabetically-scrambled, hard-to-follow order.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Because the API Scan sorts everything alphabetically, rename elements with a numerical prefix (01, 02, 03...) matching their intended TestCase execution order.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to save just the currently displayed Request message in the Payload, without saving the whole API Scan project. Which buttons should they use?

options.text: The Save/Open buttons on the Home Menu.
The Save/Load buttons in the bottom-right corner of the Payload.
There is no way to save an individual message.

practiceQuiz.hint: These buttons live right next to the payload itself, not in the ribbon.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Save and Load buttons in the bottom-right corner of the Payload save/load only the currently displayed message (request or response) — unlike the Home Menu's Save/Open, which act on the entire project.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester accidentally deletes a Message from their API Scan project and there have been no recent saves. What can they do?

options.text: Press Ctrl+Z to undo the deletion.
Nothing can bring it back except reloading the file or re-scanning the URI — there is no Undo in the API Scan.
Deleted elements are automatically archived for 24 hours.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is exactly why regular saving matters so much in the API Scan.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The API Scan has no Undo function. An accidentally deleted element can only be recovered by reloading a previously saved file or re-scanning the URI/file from scratch.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why does Tricentis recommend renaming API Scan Operations and Messages with a numerical prefix like "01", "02"?

options.text: Because the API Scan requires numeric names to export at all.
Because the API Scan sorts elements alphabetically, so numbering keeps them in the intended TestCase order.
Because Tosca Commander cannot import elements with letters in their names.
Numerical prefixes are only cosmetic and have no functional benefit.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about how the list would look without any numbering.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The API Scan automatically sorts folders, payloads, messages, and components alphabetically. Numbering them (01, 02, 03...) is the standard way to keep the sorted list matching the order they'll be used in the TestCase.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which two keyboard/menu options can rename a selected element in the API Scan?

options.text: The Rename button in the Home Menu, or pressing F2 after selecting the element.
Only the right-click context menu; there is no keyboard shortcut.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is a ribbon button, the other is a familiar Windows shortcut for renaming.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An element can be renamed either via the Rename button in the Home Menu, or by selecting it and pressing F2. Both duplicate, delete, and rename are also available via the right-click context menu.

quickRecap.value: Save / Open / Close manage the whole API Scan project.
Duplicate / Delete / Rename manipulate individual folders, operations, or messages.
Saves/loads only the currently viewed message — not the whole project.
Deleted elements can only be recovered by reloading a save or re-scanning — save often.
Home Menu > Rename, or select + F2. Right-click menu also has Duplicate/Delete/Rename.
Prefix elements 01, 02, 03... to control their alphabetically-sorted order.
